newsitem.title: NORWAY: POLL-Analysts mixed on Aker Maritime H1. [CORRECTED 11:31 GMT]
newsitem.headline: POLL-Analysts mixed on Aker Maritime H1. [CORRECTED 11:31 GMT]

text.p: Norwegian offshore supply company Aker Martime ASA is expected to post pre-tax profits of 49 million crownsfor the first half of 1997 , according to eight analysts polled by Reuters.

There were no comparitive figures for the year-ago period following the company's formation in November, 1996, after Aker ASA spun off its Oil and Gas Technology division and merged it with offshore supplier Maritime Group.
Four of the analysts recommended to buy the share, two said hold and two said sell.

The analysts gave a wide range of earnings forecasts estimates, reflecting uncertainty over the group's performance. The Total index on the Oslo bourse rose by eight percent in July, while Aker Maritime fell by one percent despite strength in the offshore sector.
Analysts' projections for the share in a 12-month horizon varied between 75 crowns and 180 crowns. At 0900 GMT on Wednesday the stock stood one crown up at 121 crowns.
Some analysts said Aker Maritime's share was now interesting following the price dip.

"Most offshore shares are now fully priced. I think there will a switch in focus from offshore services to offshore supply companies," said one analysts who had upgraded his recommendation on Aker Maritime to buy.
Others were more sceptical saying the stock had reached its top.
"When a share is too expensive, it will stand still in a rising market," commented another analyst.
One major factor affecting Aker Maritime's results is a dispute with Norsk Hydro ASA over the Njord platform and an over run in costs on the project of one billion crowns.

Hydro has refused to accept Aker's claim, and Aker is expected to take a provision of 120 million crowns for the project in the second quarter resulting in an overall loss to the company in the three-month period.
Aker Maritime will present first-half 1997 results at 0715 GMT on Thursday (Corrects day from Wednesday). Following lists analysts' expectations for the six months to June 30:
